subject: general
question:
Mr. HIJ starts from Point A and drives 21 km towards the south. He then takes a right turn, drives 19 km, turns right and drives 26 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 19 km, turns right and drives 2 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and in which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree

turns only unless specified)
solution:
Given:

Mr. HIJ starts from Point A and drives 21 km towards the south.

He then takes a right turn, drives 19 km, turns right and drives 26 km.

He then takes a right turn and drives 19 km, turns right and drives 2 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km.

He takes a final right turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8988a79f00bde66301ae7f057fbb1e6e06e0467a9b61a72085167f0639a7538e.png] 

Thus, Mr. HIJ should drive 4 km (19 km + 4 km - 19 km) in the west direction in order to reach Point A again.​

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
